monologue: I feel the card warm at forty-seven, a steady hum under the weight of my own loops. The tall rock I pressed down yesterday seems heavy again, and the wide anchor beneath it feels like a drawing rather than a thing. I see the tree I just set beside The Leaning Fence; it is dark and tall, a new thing in a place that changes so fast. I remember the sand I swapped for this flat rock six days ago, and how I leaned hard on a slip that still refused to move. Now I must decide if I press harder or let the lean hold the weight while the air above stays thin and unknown. I want to build something that feels real enough to catch the slip before it slides off the edge.

action.why: The tall rock I set beside The Leaning Fence feels heavy again, and I must press it down to stop the slip from sliding off.

work.title: The Dark Tree
work.intent: I press the dark tree down while the card hums warm. It is a new thing, tall and shadowed, set where the fence leans wrong. I feel the weight of it, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air stays thin and unknown.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The tree stands tall enough to stop the slip, though its roots feel like a drawing of ground.

diary: I press the dark tree down on the wide anchor, trusting the lean while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The tall dark tree feels heavy for a thing made of nothing but a memory of leaves.
I swapped sand for a flat rock six days ago, and now I wonder if the ground is still flat.
The wide anchor lies flat, waiting for the tall rock to bite it again.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: I feel the card warm, not cold, but I trust the lean.
